summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, and alcohol dependence was admitted for chest pain, bilateral foot pain, and suprapubic pain after losing his medications and being homeless. He presented with sharp, non-exertional chest pain and elevated BNP, indicating heart failure exacerbation, managed with IV furosemide and reinitiation of home heart failure medications. His chest pain was determined to be atypical and non-ischemic, with normal EKGs and negative troponins. Bilateral foot pain, related to prior amputations and neuropathy, was evaluated with X-rays showing no osteomyelitis but possible gout-related changes; podiatry recommended non-opioid pain management with tramadol and Lyrica. Suprapubic pain following a recent GI bleed was assessed with ultrasound, which ruled out hernia, and he was discharged on omeprazole. He expressed readiness to stop drinking, was monitored for withdrawal with CIWA and thiamine, and was connected with social work for shelter placement and sobriety resources. He was discharged home with all home medications, including rivaroxaban, metoprolol, and inhalers, and a follow-up appointment.
